svg.title: Three ways a crack can run through brickwork and what each one indicates
svg.desc: Three brick wall panels compared side by side. The first shows a stepped crack that zig-zags up and across through the mortar joints in a staircase pattern, the usual sign that one part of the wall has moved relative to another. The second shows a straight diagonal crack that breaks through the bricks themselves rather than following the joints, indicating higher or faster stress. The third shows a horizontal crack running along a single bed joint at mid height, the pattern associated with corroding cavity wall ties rather than ground movement.
